On that launch an explicit sync re-downloads the files not yet adopted (CCR-K1), and the lookups miss them (step 3's residual). issues.area: test robustness: a WP-K test fails under TSan, so the --full TSan step fails (G2/G4, Definition of Done)
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetCompatibilityTests/MigrationLaunchShimTests.swift:87 (`let legacyLeft = try launch.legacyFilesLeft()`) and :91 (`#expect(legacyLeft == 0, "every prior-art file left the prior art's tree")`), test `launchSyncDuringLegacyMigration` (the CCR-K1 tripwire)
issues.problem: The strict check `legacyLeft == 0` races the end of legacy migration. The CCR-K1 run downloads some prior-art files. Their legacy copies leave the tree only when the migration loop reaches them or phase 4 runs, which happens asynchronously after the per-asset resolves have returned. Under TSan the test reads the tree first. Full TSan run of the compatibility target: `✘ Test run with 69 tests in 10 suites failed after 1.478 seconds with 2 issues (including 1 known issue)`, with `MigrationLaunchShimTests.swift:91:9: Expectation failed: legacyLeft == 0 … legacyLeft → 2` (downloaded → 2). Re-runs of MigrationLaunchShimTests under TSan: 5 of 6 failed the same way (legacyLeft 1, 1, 1, 1, 2; downloaded 2 each). No ThreadSanitizer report in any run. Probe ProbeLegacyLeftover under TSan, 6 of 6 runs: `downloaded=2 leftAfterSync=2 leftAfterResolves=2 yields=1..3 leftAfterYields=0`, so the copies disappear one to three scheduler turns later with no clock move. It is a timing race, not files that are never removed. On a quiet host without TSan, 6 of 6 runs gave `leftAfterResolves=0`. `Scripts/quality-gates.json` has `tests.tsan = True`, so `verify.sh --full` runs this test under TSan and will usually end in `VERIFY: FAIL`. The close-out's required run of the target under TSan fails the same way. The K evidence has no TSan run of this round-2 test.
issues.fix: Make the post-condition deterministic, test first, with this TSan failure as the failing evidence. (1) From `source.starts`, compared with `CompatFixture.transfer(asset)`, find which assets were downloaded. (2) Assert strictly that every other asset's legacy file is gone. Adoption renames the file before its record is present, so this already holds when the resolves return; the lookups test pins the same with 0 transfers and passes under TSan. (3) Check the downloaded assets' legacy copies only inside the CCR-K1 `withKnownIssue` block, or drop that check. Those copies linger only because of the CCR-K1 downloads, and after the engine fix there are none. Do not wait for `.syncStarted(_, .launch)` as a signal that migration ended: when migration ends while the explicit run is still active, `startRun` returns without starting the parked launch run (Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineRuns.swift:72-74). Then run the compatibility target several times under TSan, plus verify.sh --full's TSan step.

issues.fix: The orchestrator rules on CCR-K1 as k.md's header proposes. Either (a) performSync joins the run that the migration loop's defer starts while `state.migration.running` (or pending and not deferred), instead of starting one, or (b) bulk jobs try `store.adoptLegacyNow` before transferring a record whose legacy file is still pending. The ruling may also defer it, with a record. The ruling must authorise the edit to WP-F's files, add WP-F's direct test, and remove WP-K's `withKnownIssue` wrapper once the fix lands. Note for (a): `startRun` is a no-op while a run is active (EngineRuns.swift:72-74), so the parked launch run must be handled when an explicit run overlaps migration's end.

issues.area: doc accuracy (proven by probe): the migration window is scoped to 'the first launch after adoption', and step 4 says the launch sync is 'harmless on later launches'
issues.location: docs/MIGRATION.md:38-44 (step 3), :65-72 (step 4, 'is harmless on later launches'), :155-157 and :179-181 (§4); docs/adr-drafts/k.md K-7 (:226-228), K-11 (:297-300), K-15 (:348-383), CCR-K1 header (:25-40); doc comments at Shims/CDNLocalStore.swift:15-19, :180-181, :192-193, :211-212, Shims/CDNConfiguration.swift:120-122, Shims/CDNSyncCoordinator.swift:88-92, :113-115
issues.problem: Legacy migration resumes on any later launch that finds it unfinished. StoreMigration.swift:7-11 rebuilds the plan when the persisted phase is `inProgress` and reports legacyMigrationPending, and EngineLifecycle.swift:313-320 restarts it after start(). That launch behaves exactly like the first one. Probe ProbeResumedMigration, 5 of 5 runs: launch 1 runs step 3, then the app is terminated (shutdown) during migration, leaving 149 of 150 files unadopted. On launch 2, right after start(), the lookups answered 1 of 150, and the prior art's launch `syncIfNeeded()` downloaded 6, 11, 34, 31 and 5 prior-art files (progress `.complete`, tree empty at the end). On a device, phase 2 hashes every prior-art byte, so an interrupted first launch is plausible. The unconditional advice in step 4 (no launch-task sync until CCR-K1 is fixed) still protects an adopter. But the scope statements and 'harmless on later launches' are false, and an app that resolves the prior art's videos only 'on that launch' (step 3) would miss them on the resumed launch.
issues.fix: Rescope every listed passage to 'any launch on which legacy migration is still adopting the prior art's files: the first launch after adoption, and any later launch that resumes a migration an earlier launch did not finish'. Drop or qualify 'harmless on later launches'. Optionally pin it with a shim test, using ProbeResumedMigration as the template: start, then shutdown, then relaunch over the same fakes; the lookups miss and resolves adopt.

issues.area: behaviour parity / doc gap: lifetime of the URL existingLocalURL hands out (ADR-017 consumer contract)
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetCompatibilityTests/Shims/CDNLocalStore.swift:175-185 (existingLocalURL doc); docs/MIGRATION.md §4 (:146-191) and k.md K-11; module contract at Sources/ZTronAssetModel/Reports/AssetLocation.swift:13-16 and ADR-035 (deletionGrace 10 s of awake time)
issues.problem: Not probed: this follows from the module's documented contract. The prior art kept an asset at one pretty path and replaced its bytes in place when the content changed (prior-art CDNLocalStore.swift:212-228), so a URL a page held stayed valid. The shims hand out content-addressed blob URLs. A content change gives a new URL, and the old blob may be removed `deletionGrace` (10 s of awake time by default) after the snapshot without it is installed, unless a lease holds it (AssetLocation's doc). BasicVideoPage builds its TinyVideoPlayer from the URL at init (BasicVideoPage.swift:56-62), so a page created before a republish, prune or eviction may later re-read a path that is gone. Neither the existingLocalURL doc nor MIGRATION §4 tells the adopter.
issues.fix: Add a line to MIGRATION §4 (and to K-11 or the existingLocalURL doc). The URL names the stored content. When the content changes, or the asset is pruned or evicted, the old file is removed `StoragePolicy.deletionGrace` after the new snapshot (ADR-017). A consumer that re-reads the path later, such as BasicVideoPage's player, should look it up again on failure or hold a lease (`AssetClient.withAsset`).

issues.problem: K-8 says a retry registered while online 'waits for the next path change'. The shim actually runs pending retries on the next satisfied conditions report. The live source emits one on every path change and also on every Low Power Mode and thermal-state notification. The existing test shows this: NetworkMonitorShimTests.swift:132-136 re-sends an identical `.unrestricted` and retry 2 runs. ZTronSVGView re-registers after each failure, so an SVG that keeps failing also retries on power and thermal changes, where the prior art's NWPathMonitor retried only on path updates. The impact is low.
issues.fix: State it in K-8, the MIGRATION §2 row and the monitor's doc comment. Alternatively, for closer parity, run retries only on the first report and on reports whose `network` differs from the previous one.

author_open: Deviation from the task text, for the orchestrator (K-8): NetworkAvailabilityMonitor watches the module's reachability source (AssetEnvironment.conditions; `shared` uses AssetEnvironment.live().conditions), not an AssetClient's events. An idle client observes nothing (R-SYN-14, EngineConditions.swift), and the prior art registers its retry exactly when the client has given up on the asset. The failing test c623b34 proved the event-driven version never fires then.

The shim test harness (K-10) wraps ManualTimeSource in AutoAdvancingClock. All time comes from the manual clock: sleeps due within 1 s move it automatically, and the harness sets manifestFetchDeadline to 1e6. KitHarness's fenced clock driver needs @testable engine state, which this target cannot import. A verifier should judge this against the rule 'ManualTimeSource only'.

NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW, shim API and behaviour: K-2 the install point is write-once, so CDNAssetResolver.installed = nil and re-installation are ignored. K-3 CDNLocalStore's lookups are @MainActor; the prior-art call sites are main-actor and compile, which PriorArtCallSiteTests pins. K-5 the providers no longer download (CDNShimError.downloadsGoThroughTheClient), and the client's Apple tier reads its catalog from the essential pack, not from BackgroundAssetsCDNProvider(catalog:). K-6 the deprecated initialisers build one client per install point from the first provider; a custom CDNProvidingi is never used as a transport.

Observation (K-7, nothing changed): CDNSyncProgress(outcome:) maps a `.complete` run whose manifest fetch passed its deadline (manifestFresh false) to `.complete`, although no stamp is written. The next launch retries, so the prior art's retry behaviour holds; the Stage 1 contract body was left as is.

Behaviour differences inherited from the module and pinned by shim tests (K-11): after a 404 for an asset's new content, the old bytes are no longer served (ADR-032, L4-R16); the prior art kept the old file. The extension filter also applies to manifest-known assets (ADR-037). An on-demand resolve downloads before checking the extension.
For the merge: put the proposed REENTRANCY rows k-1…k-3 (main-actor awaits in CDNSyncCoordinator, a test-target type) into ARCHITECTURE §10. Credit the 51 new R-CAR-6 test names in §11's R-CAR-6 row.
Optional, not a contract change request (K-13): a public read of the client's applied manifest would make cachedAsset(forIdentifier:) faithful and let verifyFullyAvailable() work without a provider.

Not verified here: Q-10, the adoption inside ZTronCarouselCore (ADR-006); the live monitor and StaticManifestCDNProvider against real networks; the shims at run time below the iOS 17 test-bundle target (only typechecked at iOS 15 and macOS 12).

fix_contract: CCR-K1 (WP-F engine, behaviour only, no signature change; blocking R-STO-11 for a sync requested during legacy migration). SyncEngine.performSync (Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineRuns.swift:10-39) reaches startRun(trigger: .explicit, mode:) at :39 without reading state.migration.running. start() (EngineLifecycle.swift) settles at :317, spawns the migration at :320 and parks only the launch run (launchRunWaiting, :331). Bulk jobs never try store.adoptLegacyNow, which runs only on the resolve path (EngineCommands.swift:56). Result: CDNSyncCoordinator.syncIfNeeded() or verifyAndRepair() called right after start() on the first launch after adoption downloads every prior-art file that phase 2 has not adopted yet (6 to 41 of 150 in 15 of 15 quiet runs). Minimal change, WP-F's choice: (a) while migration is running (or pending and not deferred), performSync sets launchRunWaiting and joins the run that the migration loop's defer starts (EngineRuns.swift:1055-1058); or (b) before a bulk job starts a transfer for a record whose legacy file is still pending, it tries store.adoptLegacyNow, as awaitAsset does. Tripwire: 'R-CAR-6: a coordinator's syncIfNeeded right after start on the first launch after adoption completes and downloads none of the prior art's files (CCR-K1)'. Remove its withKnownIssue wrapper with the fix. WP-F's F-8 pins only the launch run, so the direct case also needs a WP-F test. Details: docs/adr-drafts/k.md header and K-15.
